# Sirach Chapter 39 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 39 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_039_page_001.jpg

---

39:1 But the person who devotes himself to the study of the law of the Most High will seek the wisdom of all the ancients and occupy himself with prophecies.

39:2 He will preserve the discourse of famous men and penetrate the subtleties of figures of speech.

39:3 He will investigate the hidden meaning of proverbs and be occupied with the riddles of parables.

39:4 He will serve among the great and appear before rulers; he will travel through the lands of foreign peoples, for he tests what is good and evil in human experience.

39:5 He will apply his heart to rising early to seek the Lord who made him, and will pray before the Most High; he will open his mouth in prayer and supplicate for his sins.

39:6 If the great Lord wills it, he will be filled with the spirit of understanding; he will pour out his own words of wisdom and give thanks to the Lord in prayer.

39:7 He will direct his counsel and knowledge aright, and meditate on the Lord's mysteries.

39:8 He will reveal instruction in his teaching and will take pride in the law of the Lord's covenant.

39:9 Many will praise his wisdom, and it will never be erased; his memory will not be wiped away, and his name will live on through all generations.

39:10 Nations will tell of his wisdom, and the congregation will proclaim his praise.

39:11 If he lives long, he will leave behind a name greater than a thousand, and if he enters into rest, that is enough for him.

39:12 I still have more to say, which I have thought through, and I am as full as the moon at its full.

39:13 Listen to me, O holy children, and bud like a rose planted by a flowing stream;

39:14 spread your fragrance like incense, and put forth flowers like a lily. Let your voice carry sweetness and bless the Lord for all his works.

39:15 Ascribe greatness to his name and give him thanks with praise, with songs on your lips and with stringed instruments; and this is what you shall say when giving thanks:

39:16 "All the works of the Lord are very good, and every command of his will be carried out at the right time."

39:17 No one can say, "What is this?" or "Why has that happened?" — for at the right time all things will be examined. At his word the waters stood up in a heap, and the reservoirs of water at the command of his mouth.

39:18 At his word everything that pleases him is accomplished, and no one can restrict his saving power.

39:19 The deeds of all flesh are before him, and nothing can be concealed from his eyes.

39:20 From everlasting to everlasting he beholds them, and nothing is marvelous to him.

39:21 No one can say, "What is this?" or "Why has that happened?" — for all things have been made with a purpose.

39:22 His blessing covers the dry land like a river, and floods it like the Nile.

39:23 As he turned a well-watered land into salt flats, so his wrath strips nations of their heritage.

39:24 His ways are smooth to the holy, but to the wicked they are full of obstacles.

39:25 Good things were created from the beginning for good people, just as evil things were made for sinners.

39:26 The basic necessities of human life are water, fire, iron, and salt, wheat flour, milk, and honey, the juice of the grape, oil, and clothing.

39:27 All these are good for the devout, but they turn into evils for sinners.

39:28 There are winds that were created for punishment, and in their fury they can uproot mountains; in the time of annihilation they pour out their strength and appease the wrath of their Maker.

39:29 Fire and hail and famine and pestilence — all these have been made for purposes of punishment;

39:30 teeth of wild beasts, scorpions and vipers, and the avenging sword for the destruction of the wicked;

39:31 all these will rejoice in his commands, and they stand ready on earth for his service; when their season comes, they will not be lacking.

39:32 Therefore, from the beginning I was fully persuaded, and after reflecting I have set this down in writing:

39:33 all the works of the Lord are good, and he supplies every need in its proper time.

39:34 No one can say, "This is worse than that," for all things will prove good in their due season.

39:35 So now sing praises with all your heart and voice, and bless the name of the Lord.
